newsitem.title: USA: NYNEX service record stands as issue for states.
newsitem.headline: NYNEX service record stands as issue for states.

text.p: States with authority to approve NYNEX Corp's plan to merge with Bell Atlantic Corp said on Monday that NYNEX's customer-service record stands as a central issue in their consideration.
But the New England states of Maine, New Hampshire and Vermont said the company's service quality is probably not an obstacle to final approval of the $20 billion merger.

New York's Public Service Commission is leading the charge against the company's allegedly poor service record in the state. The other states involved said the issue of customer service was indeed most critical to New York.
At a hearing last month, the New York commission chairman, John O'Mara, said he was "extremely concerned" about service quality.

"We don't have the same degree of concern as the New York commission does, but we are troubled by the deterioration of service," said Larry Lackey, a policy analyst at the Vermont Department of Public Service.

He said the department was hoping the merger would help stem what it considered to be a backward slide in service quality. He said Vermont planned to continue its strategy of negotiating with NYNEX on the issues of speedy repair and maintenance.
"I am inclined to say we are not going to make a big issue of it for the merger," he said.

Customer service "will surely be a focus in the upcoming months here," said Brian Cornwall, a spokesperson of the Maine Public Utilities Commission. But he said the NYNEX service record for the state was good overall.
"NYNEX has historically had a very good level of service quality in the state of Maine," Cornwall said.
There is a public hearing scheduled November 4 for Maine residents, and the commission is scheduled to vote on the merger December 30, he said.
New Hampshire's first public hearing is scheduled for September 27. Thomas Getz, executive director of the New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission, said the service issue was sure to come up.
"Service quality would be an issue that would be raised," he said. "But it is certainly too early to say whether customer service will be an obstacle," to approval for the merger, he said.
In addition to New York and Connecticut, these three states have asserted their statutory authority to approve the merger, and any of them could seek to block the deal.
NYNEX and Bell Atlantic said they aimed to complete the merger by January 1.

NYNEX said earlier Monday it had put a customer service improvement program in place and it was already showing results. The company also said it was committed to spend an additional $1 billion on infrastructural improvements during the next five years.
